key_insight: A 0.55T prostate MRI protocol can meet PI-RADS requirements and still produce diagnostic-quality images with lesion detection performance close to 3T.
clinical_relevance: Low-field MRI could broaden access to prostate imaging by reducing scanner cost and complexity while preserving clinically usable results.
method: 15 healthy volunteers were scanned to optimize a PI-RADS-compliant bi-parametric protocol at 0.55T.
22 patients with suspected prostate cancer underwent 0.55T MRI, with 3T used as the reference standard.
Deep learning reconstruction and adjusted diffusion settings were used to improve image quality and efficiency.
evidence_signal: Most participants achieved acceptable diagnostic quality (PI-QUAL ≥2/3), and patient-level lesion detection at 0.55T was not significantly different from 3T.
watch_item: Results come from a small, single-study cohort, so broader validation is needed before routine implementation across sites.
paper_title: Feasibility of PI-RADS Compliant Prostate MRI at 0.55T
